$comment: Advisories that do NOT gate CI, with a written justification and a hard expiry.
Adding an entry here is a deliberate, reviewable act — never a silent suppression.
- An entry suppresses ONLY the named advisory in the named workspace.
- Past `expires` the entry STOPS suppressing and the gate goes red, forcing a
re-review. Bump the date only with a fresh justification.
- An entry that no longer matches any advisory is reported as stale (warning),
so cleanup is prompted once upstream ships a fix.
Only ever allowlist something that is genuinely not exploitable in this app.
'It is inconvenient to upgrade' is not a justification.

allow.reason: RSC-mode-only CSRF bypass. Darkwatch is a Vite SPA using react-router in DECLARATIVE mode (BrowserRouter + Routes/Route); it does not use React Server Components. Verified no RSC surface exists in client/src: no unstable_RSC, createCallServer, RSCHydratedRouter, and no @vitejs/plugin-rsc dependency. The vulnerable code path is therefore unreachable in this application. No fix is available on the React 18 line: react-router 7.18.1 is the last 7.x and is in the vulnerable range, while every 8.x release requires React >=19.2.7. Clearing this properly means a React 18 -> 19 upgrade, tracked in the issue above.

Dev-only, and the offered 'fix' is destructive. tmp reaches this repo ONLY through @lhci/cli@0.15.1 (its own tmp@0.1.0, plus tmp@0.0.33 via inquirer@6.5.2 -> external-editor). npm's fixAvailable is @lhci/cli@0.1.0 flagged isSemVerMajor — a DOWNGRADE of Lighthouse CI to a 2019-era release, so `npm audit fix --force` would break the Lighthouse jobs to silence this. The root workspace has zero runtime dependencies ("dependencies": {}), so nothing here is installed in the production image or reachable by a user; the advisory is exercised only when Lighthouse CI runs, in CI, over our own inputs. Clearing it properly needs @lhci/cli to modernise inquirer, or for us to drop @lhci/cli — tracked in the issue above.

Dev-only, and no override is safe. js-yaml@3.14.2 is pulled solely by @lhci/utils@0.15.1 (under @lhci/cli). The vulnerable range is <=3.14.2, so clearing it means forcing 4.x/5.x onto a 3.x consumer — and js-yaml 4 REMOVED safeLoad/safeDump, the exact API a 3.x caller uses, so the override would likely break lhci at runtime rather than fix it. Same containment as the tmp entry above: the root workspace ships nothing ("dependencies": {}), and this code path only runs when Lighthouse CI does. Tracked in the issue above.
